clue.text: Fag's boxers possibly stiff

parts.note: boxers are a breed of dog, so 'possibly' marks them as an example of dogs
a stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body

explanation.surface: A schoolboy servant's underpants are suggestively described as rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: In British public schools a fag was a junior boy who ran errands for a senior; 'boxers' are the dogs, not shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody does menial chores for others, exactly the role of a school fag serving an older pupil.

clue.text: Unreliable Archer's release about "yard near end of prison"

indicators.note: about means the release wraps around the letters that follow

parts.note: what an archer releases is an arrow's flight; also a nod to Jeffrey Archer leaving prison
by means near, as in 'stand by'

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word prison

parts.note: its last letter is N

explanation.surface: A Private Eye jibe at Jeffrey Archer's release from jail, with a teasing quote about the prison yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Archer, novelist and Tory peer, was jailed for perjury; the surface plays on that, but here the archer simply looses an arrow in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-by-night person or business is untrustworthy, liable to vanish overnight to dodge debts.

clue.text: Shag? Do this, chaps, and there's no chance!

definitions.text: Shag? Do this, chaps, and there's no chance!

parts.words: Shag? Do this, chaps, and there's no chance!
parts.note: the phrase is slang for having sex, but read literally as cutting the member off, men who did so would have no chance of it

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings collide: the slang phrase for sex, and a literal instruction to remove 'it', which would end any prospect of sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang phrase means to have sexual intercourse, the same as the vulgar verb shag.

clue.text: Lady's fingers helping to make Cook randy

indicators.note: helping to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An aphrodisiac vegetable is credited with arousing the chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies' fingers is the British name for the green seed pods also called gumbo.

clue.text: Reading fan's work out in middle of bang

indicators.note: in middle of places the rearranged letters inside the word for a bang

parts.note: a boom is a loud bang

indicators.note: out signals the word work is knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A keen reader's work explodes with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the English town but is the activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookworm is a person devoted to reading, a lover of books.

clue.text: Pisspoor Sun scoff: "Out an MP!"

indicators.note: pisspoor means wretchedly done, so the letters of the paper's name are botched into a new order

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A swipe at a tabloid's crude headline demanding a politician be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper owned by Rupert Murdoch.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat a Member of Parliament is to remove them from their seat at an election.

clue.text: Our old leader ("England's heart") is tripe

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia in England, an old English ruler

indicators.note: heart means the central letter of the country's name, the fourth of its seven

parts.note: the country's name as written, without the possessive

explanation.surface: A former British leader billed as the heart of England is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa, the Anglo-Saxon king who built Offa's Dyke, is the old leader; the middle of ENGLAND gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is stomach lining, a type of offal, the edible entrails of a slaughtered animal.

clue.text: Low-life Murdoch showing a bit of leg

indicators.note: showing says the answer is on display inside the words, across their join

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The media mogul, cast as a lowlife, flashes some leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Murdoch, owner of The Sun, is a Private Eye target; his name just carries the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, the long bone in the upper part of the leg.

clue.text: Fanny Blue's arse-kicking

parts.note: crack is vulgar slang for the female genitals, as is fanny in British English
down and blue both mean depressed, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A rude tale about someone's rear getting a kicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a severe punitive campaign, a forceful clamping down, which is a figurative kicking.

clue.text: Bloody thick, this Conservative group

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A jab calling a Tory group really stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody thick' reads as a swear plus 'stupid'; it also hints at blood that has thickened.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is a lump of thickened blood, and also an idiot, someone thick.

clue.text: L. Kelly of "the feet", bosom heaving hardly viewed as an A-list celeb

definitions.text: hardly viewed as an A-list celeb

indicators.note: heaving suggests tossing and churning, so all these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid snipe at a TV presenter's feet and heaving bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorraine Kelly is a British breakfast-television presenter; her initial and surname join the rest of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor TV presenter is just an ordinary man familiar from television, nobody important or famous.

clue.text: 'Lush arse' little Kylie's inexpressibly excruciating no.Is

indicators.note: number ones means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An insult at a pop singer's tuneless chart-toppers.
explanation.walkthrough: The words appear to describe Kylie Minogue's number one hits, but their initial letters are what count.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush is slang for a heavy drinker, and an alkie is an alcoholic.

clue.text: Rowing with one in the middle of organ stimulation

indicators.note: in the middle of places the numeral within the stirred-up letters of organ
stimulation means stirring up, so the letters of organ are agitated into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A saucy picture of rowing while being aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stimulation' stirs ORGAN into OARNG, and 'in the middle of' slips I between its R and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaring is propelling a boat with oars, which is exactly what rowing is.

clue.text: The caner first needs to get this project

definitions.text: The caner first needs to get this
definitions.meaning: someone about to cane must first get the ...

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as a schoolmaster preparing a beating; the phrase is a stick taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick out is to protrude or jut, which is one meaning of the verb project.

clue.text: "Going down" for Brenda is shaking with urgency, tense inside

indicators.note: inside means the abbreviation is set within the rearranged letters
shaking means the letters are rattled about into a new order

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: The Queen trembles urgently as she goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye nicknames Queen Elizabeth II Brenda; 'Going down' is in quotes because it is a curtsey, not anything ruder.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtseying is bending the knees in a bow, a lowering of the body as a formal courtesy.

clue.text: Taking the piss out of Joy after screwing

indicators.note: after places the word for joy behind the word for screwing

parts.note: poking is crude slang for having sex, as is screwing
fun means enjoyment, joy

explanation.surface: Mocking someone's post-coital happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking fun means mocking or ridiculing, and taking the piss is British slang for mockery.

clue.text: Eye reader joins National Guard, being sproggish

parts.note: the reader of Private Eye, where the puzzle appears, is you
NG is the abbreviation for National Guard

explanation.surface: A magazine reader signs up with the military, being childish.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle runs in Private Eye, so the Eye reader is the solver; a sprog is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sproggish is a jokey adjective from sprog, a child, so it means youthful.

clue.text: Getting an erection is a revolting thing!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rising up, read as a body part rising
second meaning: a revolt, a rebellion

explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgust but means rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a popular rebellion, and literally the act of rising up.

clue.text: See 10
Blinking fast sex — relax!

parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement, the fast flicking of eyes during sleep
it is a coy word for sex, as in 'doing it'

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to calm down during rapid-eye passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to slacken or ease off, as a fever or pain remits.

clue.text: See 10
Is a broadcaster having a drug experience here in jungle clearing?

definitions.note: a place where planes land in a cleared patch of forest

parts.note: one who broadcasts airs a programme
a trip is a hallucinogenic drug experience

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a DJ is hallucinating out in the jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a rough runway, often hacked out of forest for light aircraft to land.

clue.text: Bloody channel being pretentiously creative about Brenda

indicators.note: about means the arty word goes round the royal letters

parts.note: arty means affectedly artistic
Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose cipher is ER

explanation.surface: An arty TV channel making pretentious programmes about the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina; Brenda is Private Eye's name for her.
explanation.definitionFit: An artery is a vessel carrying blood from the heart, literally a channel for blood.

clue.text: Mind-shattering, PCs — yeh!

indicators.note: shattering breaks the letters into pieces to reassemble in a new order

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic cheer at computers being smashed, or blowing one's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or spirit, the mental self.

clue.text: Influence, power shown by Conservative/ Liberal leaders? Not the fashion!

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of the two party names

parts.note: out means unfashionable, the opposite of in

explanation.surface: Political chiefs showing off their power while out of style.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is political weight, the ability to sway decisions.

clue.text: Robin's predecessor, this member?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word before Robin in the nursery rhyme 'Who Killed ... Robin?'
second meaning: slang for the penis, a male member

explanation.walkthrough: 'predecessor' suggests an earlier holder of a job, but it just means the word that comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is vulgar slang for the male organ, and a rooster, as in the nursery rhyme bird.

clue.text: Ear nibbler gets stony reaction

indicators.note: a reaction rearranges substances, so the letters are re-formed in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone nibbling an ear gets a cold response.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer Mike Tyson bit off part of Evander Holyfield's ear in a 1997 fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavyweight champion famously bit an opponent's ear during a title bout.

clue.text: Forte put in cooler — dished up crap

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says to read the letters from bottom to top
put in places the musical letter within the word for a cooler

parts.note: a fan cools things
F is the musical abbreviation for forte, loud

explanation.surface: A posh hotel chain stuck in a fridge serves up rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' gives FFAN, and 'dished up' turns it round. Forte was also a British hotel and catering group; naff is British slang for tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff means tacky, cheap and worthless, much like the slang adjective crap.

clue.text: "Lulu Orgy" (Hello!) it's full of junk

indicators.note: a lulu is something remarkable or outrageous, signalling these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity magazine headline about a pop singer's orgy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer and Hello! a British celebrity magazine; here 'Lulu' just means something outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: A glory hole is a cupboard or room where clutter is stuffed away untidily.

clue.text: It's appreciated by the better hare with nothing left during bonk

parts.note: to hare is to run fast
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: during places the letter for left within the word for bonk

parts.note: bonk is British slang for sex, the same as the vulgar verb

explanation.surface: A fast runner, having nothing left, keeps going mid-romp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is someone who bets, a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler welcomes a winning streak, a series of good fortune.

clue.text: Girl that is stripped off in southern Africa

definitions.note: points to a place in southern Africa, a noun phrase for a region

indicators.note: stripped off means those letters are removed from the girl's name

parts.note: Natalie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl strips off somewhere in southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a province on the east coast of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal.
